The geotechnical investigation for the proposed highway interchange included 20 soil borings to depths of 60 to 100 feet, 10 cone penetration tests, and laboratory testing of 85 soil samples. Subsurface conditions consist of 8 to 12 feet of sandy clay fill overlying native alluvial deposits of medium dense to dense sand and gravel. Groundwater was encountered at depths of 15 to 22 feet below existing grade. The recommended foundation system for bridge piers is 48-inch drilled shafts socketed a minimum of 10 feet into the underlying sandstone formation. Allowable bearing pressure for the sandstone is 30 ksf. Settlement analysis indicates less than 0.5 inches of total settlement under design loads. Liquefaction potential was evaluated and determined to be low based on SPT blow counts exceeding 25 in the granular deposits. Project reference: PRJ-5012.

The MBR system combines activated sludge biological treatment with ultrafiltration membrane separation, achieving effluent turbidity below 0.1 NTU and BOD5 below 2 mg per liter. Total nitrogen removal achieves less than 3 mg per liter in the effluent. Membrane flux is maintained at 15 gallons per square foot per day with chemical cleaning cycles every 90 days. Energy consumption for the MBR process is approximately 1.2 kWh per cubic meter of treated water. Project reference: PRJ-1434.
